question: What is the difference between `unique_ptr`, `shared_ptr`, and `weak_ptr`?

scenes.sub: Three smart pointers, three answers to “who owns this?”
scenes.say: Unique pointer, shared pointer, and weak pointer. They're the three smart pointers in modern C plus plus, and the whole difference is about who owns the object.

scenes.head: unique_ptr: exactly one owner
scenes.say: A unique pointer is the sole owner of its object. Here, a owns a heap int holding forty two. You can't copy a unique pointer, because then two owners would both try to delete it. You can only move it. s t d colon colon move moves ownership to b, and a is left holding null p t r. When b goes out of scope, it deletes the int. No count, and usually no overhead over a raw pointer.

scenes.head: shared_ptr counts owners, weak_ptr just watches
scenes.say: A shared pointer allows many owners. s1 creates the int, plus a control block that holds the counts. Copying into s2 bumps the strong count to two. A weak pointer observes without owning, so only the weak count goes up. When we reset s1, the strong count drops to one. When the last owner lets go, the count hits zero and the int is destroyed. The weak pointer survives, and expired returns true.

scenes.head: Using a weak_ptr: lock() it first
scenes.say: You can't use a weak pointer directly. You call lock, which gives you a shared pointer if the object is still alive, or an empty one if it's gone. Inside the block, lock succeeds and prints forty two. After the block, the last owner died, so lock fails and we print expired. That's how caches and observers check safely, and how you break shared pointer cycles.

scenes.head: Side by side
scenes.say: Ownership: unique pointer is the sole owner, shared pointer has many, and weak pointer owns nothing. Copying: unique pointer can only be moved, while copying a shared pointer adds an owner. Cost: unique pointer is usually as cheap as a raw pointer, shared pointer needs a control block with atomic counters. The object is freed when its unique owner dies, or when the last shared owner dies. And use unique pointer by default.

lines: unique_ptr: one owner, move-only, near-zero cost. Your default.
shared_ptr: reference-counted shared ownership. Freed when the last owner goes.
weak_ptr: non-owning observer. lock() to use it. Breaks cycles.
scenes.say: Unique pointer: one owner, move only, practically free. Make it your default. Shared pointer: reference counted shared ownership, freed when the last owner goes. Weak pointer: a non owning observer. You lock it to use it, and it breaks shared pointer cycles.
